content.value_statement: Python data validation can be repetitive and inconsistent. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Pydantic v2 models, validators, serialization, and schemas.
actual_capabilities: Creates Pydantic BaseModel examples with typed fields and defaults.
Applies Field constraints, aliases, descriptions, and excluded fields.
Shows ConfigDict options for strict models and assignment validation.
Demonstrates field validators and model validators for custom rules.
Explains model_dump, model_dump_json, include, exclude, and alias serialization.
Covers nested models, enums, TypeAdapter, and validation error handling.
limitations: Does not include runnable project scaffolding or package files.
Does not cover database integrations or web framework adapters.
Does not include BaseSettings examples despite mentioning settings management.
Examples are instructional and should be tested against project requirements.

use_cases.title: Model API Requests
use_cases.description: Define request and response models with field constraints, aliases, and validation errors.

use_cases.title: Validate Data Pipelines
use_cases.description: Create typed validation layers for imported records, nested structures, and enum values.

use_cases.title: Standardize Serialization
use_cases.description: Control exported fields, secret handling, aliases, and JSON-compatible output formats.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Pydantic v2 model for [data object]. Include field types, required fields, default values, and simple validation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Constraints and Validators
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this Pydantic v2 model with Field constraints, aliases, field validators, and clear validation error behavior: [model details].

prompt_templates.title: Control Serialized Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Pydantic v2 serialization for [model]. Show which fields to include, exclude, alias, or protect from output.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Validation Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Pydantic v2 validation layer for [workflow]. Include nested models, enum handling, TypeAdapter usage, and validation error strategy.

output_examples.input: A product object needs an id alias, positive price, email contact, website URL, tags, and hidden internal data.
output_examples.output: A model plan with field constraints, alias support, default tag handling, validated contact fields, and excluded internal data.

output_examples.input: A date range model must reject empty dates and ensure the start date is before the end date.
output_examples.output: A validation approach using field-level checks for empty values and a model-level check for date ordering.

output_examples.input: A task model needs enum values, nested addresses, and safe serialized output for an API response.
output_examples.output: A design that combines enum configuration, nested Pydantic models, and controlled serialization with selected fields.

best_practices: Use specific field constraints instead of broad types when input limits are known.
Configure model behavior with ConfigDict before adding custom validators.
Test serialization choices so private fields and secrets do not appear in output.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on automatic coercion when strict validation is required.
Do not expose internal fields or secret values through default serialization.
Do not place cross-field rules in separate field validators when model validators fit better.

faq.question: What version of Pydantic does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Pydantic v2 patterns, including BaseModel, ConfigDict, validators, serialization, and TypeAdapter.

faq.question: Can it help with custom validators?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows field validators for single fields and model validators for cross-field checks.

faq.question: Does it include serialization guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers model_dump, JSON output, aliases, include rules, exclude rules, and protected fields.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. Installation commands are documentation examples and require user action outside the skill.

faq.question: Is it suitable for nested data structures?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes nested model examples for related objects and reusable schemas.

faq.question: Does it replace project-specific testing?
faq.answer: No. Generated models and validators should be tested with real project inputs and expected failures.
